blocks.text: US Policy Shift After the Midterm Elections, Market Correction and Cross-Asset Investment Opportunities
I. Executive Summary

blocks.html: In November 2026, US financial markets underwent two important changes: first, the Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, moving the US political landscape from unified Republican government to divided government; second, technology stocks centered on artificial intelligence corrected sharply, driving a repricing of risk assets.
blocks.text: In November 2026, US financial markets underwent two important changes: first, the Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the midterm elections, moving the US political landscape from unified Republican government to divided government; second, technology stocks centered on artificial intelligence corrected sharply, driving a repricing of risk assets.

blocks.html: This correction is not simply a technical pullback; it is the combined result of four factors: policy expectations, the cost of capital, the return on AI investment and market liquidity.
blocks.text: This correction is not simply a technical pullback; it is the combined result of four factors: policy expectations, the cost of capital, the return on AI investment and market liquidity.

blocks.html: Our main investment conclusions are as follows:
blocks.text: Our main investment conclusions are as follows:

items: Policy environment: Democratic control of Congress will limit the Trump administration's ability to push further large-scale fiscal expansion and some deregulatory measures, but the executive branch still retains substantial trade, foreign-policy and regulatory enforcement powers. The fiscal budget, the debt ceiling and AI regulation will be the main sources of policy uncertainty ahead.

Market environment: On November 20, the S&P 500 fell 3.7% in a single day and the Nasdaq fell 5.28%, while US Treasuries rallied. This shows the market is reducing its exposure to risk assets, but the broad credit market has not yet repriced risk to the same extent as equities.

Credit markets: IG and HY spreads have widened somewhat but remain at relatively moderate levels overall; the stress is concentrated in the low-rated tail, with CCC spreads above 1,000bps, and the energy shock has further deepened credit dispersion. Conditions for new Private Credit and ABF investments may improve, but existing assets face pressure on valuations, refinancing and credit quality.

Private Markets: Valuation adjustments in real estate and AI VC may lag the public markets. AI-related VC, data centers and GPU financing in particular carry the risk that valuations, financing and end demand are highly correlated.

Asset allocation: Over the next 6–12 months, favor credit strategies with stable Cash Yield, shorter payback periods and clear collateral protection. Keep enough Dry Powder to capture price opportunities from Secondary Credit, Whole Loans and special financing needs.

blocks.html: Overall view: the market is more likely to enter a phase of valuation adjustment and asset dispersion lasting several months than to quickly return to the broad rally previously driven by AI.
blocks.text: Overall view: the market is more likely to enter a phase of valuation adjustment and asset dispersion lasting several months than to quickly return to the broad rally previously driven by AI.
II. The Midterm Elections: A Structural Change in the US Policy Environment
2.1 Election Results and the Policy Landscape

blocks.html: In the midterm elections of November 3, 2026, the Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, and will control the 120th Congress from January 3, 2027.
blocks.text: In the midterm elections of November 3, 2026, the Democrats won control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, and will control the 120th Congress from January 3, 2027.

blocks.html: This result means the Trump administration will face stronger congressional oversight and legislative checks for the rest of its term.
blocks.text: This result means the Trump administration will face stronger congressional oversight and legislative checks for the rest of its term.

blocks.html: It should be stressed that Democratic control of Congress does not mean existing tax, trade and industrial policies can be overturned unilaterally. The President still holds the veto, and major legislation in the Senate may also be constrained by procedural rules.
blocks.text: It should be stressed that Democratic control of Congress does not mean existing tax, trade and industrial policies can be overturned unilaterally. The President still holds the veto, and major legislation in the Senate may also be constrained by procedural rules.

blocks.html: Policy changes over the next two years are therefore more likely to take the form of:
blocks.text: Policy changes over the next two years are therefore more likely to take the form of:

items: new fiscal stimulus and large-scale tax reform becoming harder;
stronger congressional oversight of executive power, tariffs and government spending;
rising regulatory pressure on AI, data centers, energy consumption and large technology companies;
a greater risk of disputes over government budget negotiations and the debt ceiling;
policy uncertainty shifting from unilateral executive decisions to bargaining between the executive and legislative branches.

blocks.text: 2.2 Main Effects on the Macroeconomy

blocks.html: Fiscal policy: from expectations of expansion to political constraints.
blocks.text: Fiscal policy: from expectations of expansion to political constraints.

blocks.html: Democratic control of Congress lowers the likelihood of further large-scale fiscal expansion, but may not significantly reduce the existing fiscal deficit.
blocks.text: Democratic control of Congress lowers the likelihood of further large-scale fiscal expansion, but may not significantly reduce the existing fiscal deficit.

blocks.html: In the long run, fiscal constraints may ease Treasury supply and inflation expectations; in the short run, they may raise the risk of a government budget impasse.
blocks.text: In the long run, fiscal constraints may ease Treasury supply and inflation expectations; in the short run, they may raise the risk of a government budget impasse.

blocks.html: Trade and inflation: tariff policy remains uncertain.
blocks.text: Trade and inflation: tariff policy remains uncertain.

blocks.html: Congress may strengthen its oversight of tariff policy, but the Trump administration still retains some executive trade authority.
blocks.text: Congress may strengthen its oversight of tariff policy, but the Trump administration still retains some executive trade authority.

blocks.html: The market should therefore not assume that the midterm elections will quickly remove tariff and supply-chain cost pressures.
blocks.text: The market should therefore not assume that the midterm elections will quickly remove tariff and supply-chain cost pressures.

blocks.html: AI regulation: an important change in future policy risk.
blocks.text: AI regulation: an important change in future policy risk.

blocks.html: Democrats may focus more on data-center energy consumption, consumer protection, data privacy, AI safety and the effect on employment.
blocks.text: Democrats may focus more on data-center energy consumption, consumer protection, data privacy, AI safety and the effect on employment.

blocks.html: For AI companies this does not necessarily mean lower revenue directly, but it may raise compliance costs, lengthen construction timelines for data-center projects and affect the return on future CapEx.
blocks.text: For AI companies this does not necessarily mean lower revenue directly, but it may raise compliance costs, lengthen construction timelines for data-center projects and affect the return on future CapEx.

blocks.html: In our view, changes in AI regulation and in the return on capital expenditure are the cross-cutting risk of these midterm elections that matters most for financial markets.

III. Equity and Bond Markets: From Growth Optimism to Risk Repricing
3.1 Equity Market

blocks.text: As of November 20:

blocks.html: Technology and semiconductor stocks significantly underperformed the broad market, reflecting that positions previously concentrated in AI Growth are being cut.
blocks.text: Technology and semiconductor stocks significantly underperformed the broad market, reflecting that positions previously concentrated in AI Growth are being cut.

blocks.html: We see the market's main concerns as:
blocks.text: We see the market's main concerns as:

items: the long-term ROIC of AI infrastructure investment;

blocks.html: The key to this correction is that even if AI revenue keeps growing, valuations can still compress significantly as long as growth is slower than the expectations previously implied by share prices.

3.2 Rates and the Treasury Market

blocks.html: On November 20, the 2-year and 10-year US Treasury yields were about 4.63% and 4.92% respectively, both falling markedly on the day.
blocks.text: On November 20, the 2-year and 10-year US Treasury yields were about 4.63% and 4.92% respectively, both falling markedly on the day.

blocks.html: During the sharp fall in equities, the Treasury Rally showed that Treasuries still served to some extent as a safe haven and a portfolio hedge.
blocks.text: During the sharp fall in equities, the Treasury Rally showed that Treasuries still served to some extent as a safe haven and a portfolio hedge.

blocks.html: But this does not mean interest-rate risk has disappeared.
blocks.text: But this does not mean interest-rate risk has disappeared.

blocks.html: The Treasury market may be shaped by three forces at once:
blocks.text: The Treasury market may be shaped by three forces at once:

items: slower economic growth pushing yields down;
sticky inflation and Fed policy limiting room for rate cuts;
fiscal deficits and debt-ceiling disputes pushing up the Term Premium.

blocks.html: One should therefore not bet one-way on a sustained fall in long-term Treasury yields, and should keep a reasonable Duration Risk Budget.
blocks.text: One should therefore not bet one-way on a sustained fall in long-term Treasury yields, and should keep a reasonable Duration Risk Budget.
3.3 Credit Market

blocks.html: As of around November 19, IG and HY OAS were about 94bps and 352bps respectively.
blocks.text: As of around November 19, IG and HY OAS were about 94bps and 352bps respectively.

blocks.html: The widening of credit spreads so far is clearly smaller than the change in risk appetite implied by the fall in equities.
blocks.text: The widening of credit spreads so far is clearly smaller than the change in risk appetite implied by the fall in equities.

blocks.html: This points to two possibilities:
blocks.text: This points to two possibilities:

blocks.html: First, the equity market is mainly digesting previously excessive valuations, while corporate fundamentals have not deteriorated systemically.
blocks.text: First, the equity market is mainly digesting previously excessive valuations, while corporate fundamentals have not deteriorated systemically.

blocks.html: Second, risk pricing in the credit market is lagging; if earnings forecasts keep being cut, Spreads may widen further.
blocks.text: Second, risk pricing in the credit market is lagging; if earnings forecasts keep being cut, Spreads may widen further.

blocks.html: We take the first case as our base case, but the second risk must be watched closely: the low-rated tail already shows early signs of the second case (see 3.4).
blocks.text: We take the first case as our base case, but the second risk must be watched closely: the low-rated tail already shows early signs of the second case (see 3.4).
3.4 The Energy Shock and Dispersion in the Credit Tail

blocks.html: The energy shock: from inflation pressure to pressure on margins and cash flow.
blocks.text: The energy shock: from inflation pressure to pressure on margins and cash flow.

blocks.html: The energy shock caused by the 2026 disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was an important source of this year's sticky inflation, passing through to corporate margins via fuel, transport and raw-material costs. After the midterm elections, the market began to price in an easing of tensions in the Middle East and a recovery in oil supply, and WTI fell from about US$106/bbl at the end of October to about US$91/bbl in mid-November, but the geopolitical risk premium may still flare up again.
blocks.text: The energy shock caused by the 2026 disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was an important source of this year's sticky inflation, passing through to corporate margins via fuel, transport and raw-material costs. After the midterm elections, the market began to price in an easing of tensions in the Middle East and a recovery in oil supply, and WTI fell from about US$106/bbl at the end of October to about US$91/bbl in mid-November, but the geopolitical risk premium may still flare up again.

blocks.html: The energy shock does not hit the credit market evenly:
blocks.text: The energy shock does not hit the credit market evenly:

items: highly leveraged, low-margin issuers that find it hard to pass on costs (chemicals, transport, airlines, some consumer goods and retail) are hit hardest by rising input costs;
after oil prices fall from their highs, some highly leveraged upstream energy and oilfield-services issuers instead face the risk of lower revenue and cash flow;
energy prices push up inflation expectations and limit the Fed's room to cut rates, keeping the interest burden of floating-rate borrowers high.

blocks.html: Dispersion in the credit tail: CCC spreads above 1,000bps.
blocks.text: Dispersion in the credit tail: CCC spreads above 1,000bps.

blocks.html: As of mid-November, the spread on CCC-rated high-yield bonds was about 1,135bps, the highest since July 2020 and within the range usually regarded as Distress. The gap between CCC and overall HY spreads widened to nearly 10 percentage points, against about 6 percentage points a year ago. In October, BB and single-B spreads widened by only about 15bps and 30bps respectively, while CCC widened by about 108bps.

The gap between CCC and overall HY spreads widened to nearly 10 percentage points, against about 6 percentage points a year ago. In October, BB and single-B spreads widened by only about 15bps and 30bps respectively, while CCC widened by about 108bps.

blocks.html: This shows that the current stress in the high-yield market is not systemic but highly concentrated in low-rated issuers with fragile capital structures and limited refinancing windows. An overall HY OAS of about 350bps masks the tail risk to some extent.
blocks.text: This shows that the current stress in the high-yield market is not systemic but highly concentrated in low-rated issuers with fragile capital structures and limited refinancing windows. An overall HY OAS of about 350bps masks the tail risk to some extent.

blocks.html: We believe the widening of CCC spreads mainly reflects three factors:
blocks.text: We believe the widening of CCC spreads mainly reflects three factors:

items: energy and input-cost shocks combined with high rates, squeezing the Interest Coverage of low-rated companies;
debt maturities in the next 1–2 years drawing closer, raising concern about low-rated issuers' ability to refinance;
more Liability Management Exercises (LME) and Distressed Exchanges, lowering expected recovery rates.

blocks.html: Implications for the existing portfolio: CCC spreads persistently above 1,000bps usually lead a rise in default rates and may spread to borrowers with similar characteristics in Private Credit, especially Sponsor-backed, highly leveraged loans or loans that already pay PIK. Because private credit valuations adjust with a lag, the CCC spread and its gap to the overall HY spread should be used as a forward-looking signal of credit risk in the existing portfolio.

4.2 High Yield Credit

blocks.html: View: cautious in the short term, waiting for Spreads to widen further.
blocks.text: View: cautious in the short term, waiting for Spreads to widen further.

blocks.html: The current HY OAS of about 350bps does not yet fully reflect the risk of a more severe credit cycle.

blocks.html: View: cautious on existing assets; new investment opportunities improving.

4.4 Asset-Backed Finance（ABF）

blocks.html: View: one of the areas most deserving of more research and trading resources.
blocks.text: View: one of the areas most deserving of more research and trading resources.

blocks.html: The advantage of ABF is that its returns can rest directly on the cash flows of the underlying assets, Collateral Value and structural credit protection, rather than depending entirely on corporate valuation multiples.
blocks.text: The advantage of ABF is that its returns can rest directly on the cash flows of the underlying assets, Collateral Value and structural credit protection, rather than depending entirely on corporate valuation multiples.

Seconds / HELOC；

4.5 Real Estate

blocks.html: Real estate valuations depend on Treasury yields, risk premia and NOI growth at the same time.
blocks.text: Real estate valuations depend on Treasury yields, risk premia and NOI growth at the same time.

items: Cap Rates failing to fall in step with Treasury Yields;

blocks.html: Relatively speaking, SFR, Multifamily and some Industrial assets with stable occupancy, low leverage and predictable cash flow deserve more attention.

4.6 AI Venture Capital Valuations

blocks.html: View: cautious in the short term, mainly waiting for Late-stage Secondary opportunities.
blocks.text: View: cautious in the short term, mainly waiting for Late-stage Secondary opportunities.

blocks.html: The valuation risk of AI VC comes mainly from Public Market Multiple Compression and lower exit valuations.
blocks.text: The valuation risk of AI VC comes mainly from Public Market Multiple Compression and lower exit valuations.

blocks.html: Unlike listed companies, private-market valuations may adjust gradually through follow-on financings, Secondary Transactions and quarterly valuation reports.
blocks.text: Unlike listed companies, private-market valuations may adjust gradually through follow-on financings, Secondary Transactions and quarterly valuation reports.

blocks.html: We expect valuations to diverge significantly:
blocks.text: We expect valuations to diverge significantly:

items: AI companies with high cash burn and little differentiation face heavy financing and valuation pressure;
AI infrastructure companies that depend on continuous external financing bear a higher cost of capital;
AI application companies with high customer retention, real commercial revenue and stable cash flow are relatively more resilient;
scarce technology platforms may continue to command a high valuation premium.

blocks.html: We do not recommend adding VC exposure merely because of the AI theme.

VI. Portfolio Recommendations

blocks.html: Since there is currently no new capital for future investments, portfolio management over the next 6–12 months will shift its focus from new allocations to managing the existing portfolio: protecting current income with Defensive Carry, selectively capturing Dislocation opportunities with proceeds from maturing and repaid existing assets, and keeping ample Liquidity Optionality.

blocks.html: The 2026 midterm elections changed the US policy environment for the next two years, and the recent fall in AI technology stocks further triggered a repricing of risk-asset valuations.
